1	"""Placement predicates, node selection and preemption.
2	
3	Predicates are pure functions returning `(ok, reason)`: a rejection that cannot say why is useless
4	when a schedule looks wrong, so every branch names the constraint it hit. Node selection is
5	deterministic -- ties always break on node id -- and preemption picks the *smallest* set of the
6	lowest-priority tasks that makes the incoming task fit.
7	"""
8	
9	from __future__ import annotations
10	
11	from dataclasses import dataclass
12	
13	from .errors import ValidationError
14	from .model import Cluster, Node, Placement, Resources, Task
15	
16	POLICIES = ("first-fit", "best-fit")
17	
18	
19	@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
20	class Decision:
21	    task_id: str
22	    node_id: str | None
23	    reason: str
24	    preempted: tuple[str, ...] = ()
25	
26	    def to_document(self) -> dict[str, object]:
27	        document: dict[str, object] = {"task": self.task_id, "reason": self.reason}
28	        if self.node_id is not None:
29	            document["node"] = self.node_id
30	        if self.preempted:
31	            document["preempted"] = list(self.preempted)
32	        return document
33	
34	
35	def capacity_predicate(task: Task, free: Resources) -> tuple[bool, str]:
36	    if not task.request.fits(free):
37	        return False, f"insufficient capacity: needs cpu={task.request.cpu},memory={task.request.memory} has cpu={free.cpu},memory={free.memory}"
38	    return True, "capacity ok"
39	
40	
41	def affinity_predicate(task: Task, node: Node) -> tuple[bool, str]:
42	    labels = node.label_map()
43	    for key, value in task.affinity:
44	        if labels.get(key) != value:
45	            return False, f"affinity {key}={value} not satisfied (node has {key}={labels.get(key)!r})"
46	    for key in task.anti_affinity:
47	        if key in labels:
48	            return False, f"anti-affinity: node carries label {key}"
49	    return True, "affinity ok"
50	
51	
52	def taint_predicate(task: Task, node: Node) -> tuple[bool, str]:
53	    for taint in node.taints:
54	        if taint not in task.tolerations:
55	            return False, f"untolerated taint {taint}"
56	    return True, "taints ok"
57	
58	
59	PREDICATES = (capacity_predicate, affinity_predicate, taint_predicate)
60	
61	
62	def fits(cluster: Cluster, task: Task, node: Node) -> tuple[bool, str]:
63	    """All predicates, reported in a stable order so the first failure is always the same one."""
64	    free = cluster.free(node.id)
65	    ok, reason = capacity_predicate(task, free)
66	    if not ok:
67	        return False, reason
68	    ok, reason = affinity_predicate(task, node)
69	    if not ok:
70	        return False, reason
71	    return taint_predicate(task, node)
72	
73	
74	def order_candidates(cluster: Cluster, policy: str) -> list[Node]:
75	    if policy not in POLICIES:
76	        raise ValidationError(f"policy must be one of {', '.join(POLICIES)}", value=policy)
77	    nodes = sorted(cluster.nodes, key=lambda node: node.id)
78	    if policy == "first-fit":
79	        return nodes
80	    # best-fit: smallest remaining CPU, then smallest remaining memory, then node id for determinism
81	    return sorted(nodes, key=lambda node: (cluster.free(node.id).cpu, cluster.free(node.id).memory, node.id))
82	
83	
84	def select_node(cluster: Cluster, task: Task, policy: str = "first-fit") -> Decision:
85	    """The first candidate that passes every predicate, in the order the policy defines."""
86	    reasons: list[str] = []
87	    for node in order_candidates(cluster, policy):
88	        ok, reason = fits(cluster, task, node)
89	        if ok:
90	            return Decision(task.id, node.id, f"placed by {policy}")
91	        reasons.append(f"{node.id}: {reason}")
92	    detail = "; ".join(reasons) if reasons else "no nodes in the cluster"
93	    return Decision(task.id, None, f"no node fits ({detail})")
94	
95	
96	def running_on(placements: list[Placement], tasks: dict[str, Task], node_id: str, now: int) -> list[Placement]:
97	    return [item for item in placements if item.node_id == node_id and item.start <= now < item.end and item.task_id in tasks]
98	
99	
100	def preemption_candidates(
101	    cluster: Cluster,
102	    task: Task,
103	    node: Node,
104	    placements: list[Placement],
105	    tasks: dict[str, Task],
106	    now: int,
107	) -> tuple[list[Placement], str]:
108	    """The smallest set of lower-priority running tasks whose eviction frees room for `task`.
109	
110	    Candidates are ordered lowest priority first, then largest request, then task id, and the search
111	    stops as soon as the request fits -- so the answer is deterministic and is never larger than needed.
112	    A task is never a candidate for eviction of something at its own priority or higher.
113	    """
114	    if task.priority <= 0:
115	        return [], "preemption only applies to positive priorities"
116	    clock_free = cluster.free(node.id)
117	    if task.request.fits(clock_free):
118	        return [], "no preemption needed"
119	    candidates = [item for item in running_on(placements, tasks, node.id, now) if tasks[item.task_id].priority < task.priority]
120	    candidates.sort(key=lambda item: (tasks[item.task_id].priority, -tasks[item.task_id].request.cpu, -tasks[item.task_id].request.memory, item.task_id))
121	    freed = clock_free
122	    chosen: list[Placement] = []
123	    for candidate in candidates:
124	        chosen.append(candidate)
125	        freed = freed.plus(tasks[candidate.task_id].request)
126	        if task.request.fits(freed):
127	            return chosen, f"preempting {len(chosen)} lower-priority task(s) on {node.id}"
128	    return [], f"even evicting every lower-priority task on {node.id} would not fit cpu={task.request.cpu},memory={task.request.memory}"
129	
130	
131	def fragmentation(cluster: Cluster, tasks: dict[str, Task]) -> dict[str, int]:
132	    """How many nodes could not accept the smallest pending task, and their wasted CPU."""
133	    if not tasks:
134	        return {"nodesBlocked": 0, "wastedCpu": 0}
135	    smallest = min(tasks.values(), key=lambda item: (item.request.cpu, item.request.memory, item.id)).request
136	    blocked = 0
137	    wasted = 0
138	    for node in cluster.nodes:
139	        free = cluster.free(node.id)
140	        if not smallest.fits(free):
141	            blocked += 1
142	            wasted += free.cpu
143	    return {"nodesBlocked": blocked, "wastedCpu": wasted}
144

1	"""Deterministic scheduler simulation: an event clock, conservative backfill, and metrics.
2	
3	The simulator is a pure function of its input. It never consults the wall clock, never iterates a
4	`set` in a way that affects a decision, and never breaks a tie by insertion order -- so the same
5	cluster and task list always produce the same trace, and `replay` proves it instead of asserting it.
6	
7	One list holds every placement ever made; "running" is derived from the clock (`start <= t < end`),
8	which removes any chance of the bookkeeping disagreeing with the schedule. Capacity is released
9	exactly once per placement, tracked by index.
10	
11	With ``queue_weights`` supplied the run is in fair-share mode: priorities still order the waiting
12	list, but tasks of equal priority are picked from the queue with the smallest weighted dominant
13	share -- max(used CPU / total CPU, used memory / total memory) / weight -- and shares are
14	recomputed after every release, placement and preemption. Shares are kept as exact rational
15	ratios (``Fraction``), so ordering never loses precision on large integer capacities; the value
16	is rounded to six decimals only when it leaves the simulator in a trace or metric document.
17	Without that mapping, nothing changes.
18	"""
19	
20	from __future__ import annotations
21	
22	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
23	from fractions import Fraction
24	
25	from .errors import ValidationError
26	from .model import Cluster, Node, Placement, Resources, Task
27	from .policies import POLICIES, fragmentation, preemption_candidates, select_node
28	
29	
30	@dataclass(slots=True)
31	class SimulationResult:
32	    policy: str
33	    placements: list[Placement]
34	    decisions: list[dict[str, object]]
35	    unplaced: list[str]
36	    makespan: int
37	    metrics: dict[str, object]
38	
39	    def trace(self) -> list[tuple[str, str, int, int]]:
40	        """The identity of a run: (task, node, start, end) sorted -- what determinism is checked on."""
41	        return sorted((item.task_id, item.node_id, item.start, item.end) for item in self.placements)
42	
43	    def to_document(self) -> dict[str, object]:
44	        return {
45	            "policy": self.policy,
46	            "makespan": self.makespan,
47	            "placed": len(self.placements),
48	            "unplaced": self.unplaced,
49	            "metrics": self.metrics,
50	            "placements": [item.to_document() for item in self.placements],
51	        }
52	
53	
54	@dataclass(slots=True)
55	class Simulation:
56	    nodes: tuple[Node, ...]
57	    tasks: tuple[Task, ...]
58	    policy: str = "first-fit"
59	    allow_preemption: bool = False
60	    backfill: bool = True
61	    queue_weights: dict[str, int] | None = None
62	    _cluster: Cluster = field(init=False)
63	    _placements: list[Placement] = field(default_factory=list, init=False)
64	    _released: set[int] = field(default_factory=set, init=False)
65	    _decisions: list[dict[str, object]] = field(default_factory=list, init=False)
66	    _preemptions: int = field(default=0, init=False)
67	    _waits: list[int] = field(default_factory=list, init=False)
68	    _last_refusal: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict, init=False)
69	
70	    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
71	        if self.policy not in POLICIES:
72	            raise ValidationError(f"policy must be one of {', '.join(POLICIES)}", value=self.policy)
73	        ids = [task.id for task in self.tasks]
74	        if len(set(ids)) != len(ids):
75	            raise ValidationError("task ids must be unique")
76	        if self.queue_weights is not None:
77	            if not self.queue_weights:
78	                raise ValidationError("queue weights must declare at least one queue")
79	            for name, weight in self.queue_weights.items():
80	                if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
81	                    raise ValidationError("queue weights must use non-empty queue names", value=name)
82	                if isinstance(weight, bool) or not isinstance(weight, int) or weight <= 0:
83	                    raise ValidationError("queue weights must be positive integers", queue=name, value=weight)
84	        self._cluster = Cluster(self.nodes)
85	
86	    # -- bookkeeping -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
87	    @property
88	    def task_index(self) -> dict[str, Task]:
89	        return {task.id: task for task in self.tasks}
90	
91	    @property
92	    def fair(self) -> bool:
93	        return self.queue_weights is not None
94	
95	    def _weight(self, queue: str) -> int:
96	        # A queue used by a task but absent from the config carries an implicit weight of one.
97	        assert self.queue_weights is not None
98	        return self.queue_weights.get(queue, 1)
99	
100	    def _shares(self, clock: int) -> dict[str, Fraction]:
101	        """Weighted dominant share of every queue from the tasks running at ``clock``.
102	
103	        The dominant resource is the larger of the queue's CPU and memory fractions of total cluster
104	        capacity; dividing by the queue weight yields its weighted dominant share. Shares are exact
105	        rational ratios built from the integer inputs, so two shares that differ by less than one
106	        binary floating-point ulp still order correctly -- the ratio is rounded to six decimals only
107	        when it is written into a trace or metric document. A resource with zero total capacity
108	        contributes a zero fraction (never a division by zero).
109	        """
110	        assert self.queue_weights is not None
111	        running = self._active(clock)
112	        used: dict[str, Resources] = {}
113	        for item in running:
114	            task = self.task_index[item.task_id]
115	            used[task.queue] = used.get(task.queue, Resources(0, 0)).plus(task.request)
116	        capacity = self._cluster.total_capacity()
117	        shares: dict[str, Fraction] = {}
118	        for queue, request in used.items():
119	            cpu_fraction = Fraction(request.cpu, capacity.cpu) if capacity.cpu else Fraction(0)
120	            memory_fraction = Fraction(request.memory, capacity.memory) if capacity.memory else Fraction(0)
121	            shares[queue] = max(cpu_fraction, memory_fraction) / self._weight(queue)
122	        return shares
123	
124	    def _pending_order(self, pending: list[Task], clock: int) -> list[Task]:
125	        if not self.fair:
126	            return sorted(pending, key=lambda task: (-task.priority, task.arrival, task.id))
127	        shares = self._shares(clock)
128	        return sorted(
129	            pending,
130	            key=lambda task: (
131	                -task.priority,
132	                shares.get(task.queue, Fraction(0)),
133	                task.arrival,
134	                task.queue,
135	                task.id,
136	            ),
137	        )
138	
139	    def _active(self, clock: int) -> list[Placement]:
140	        return [item for item in self._placements if item.start <= clock < item.end]
141	
142	    def _running_end(self, clock: int) -> int | None:
143	        ends = [item.end for item in self._active(clock)]
144	        return min(ends) if ends else None
145	
146	    def _release_finished(self, clock: int) -> None:
147	        """Free capacity for everything that has ended by `clock`, once per placement.
148	
149	        This runs *before* placement at the same tick: capacity freed at t must be available to the
150	        task considered at t. The first version placed first and released afterwards, which held
151	        resources one tick too long.
152	        """
153	        for index, item in enumerate(self._placements):
154	            if index in self._released or item.end > clock:
155	                continue
156	            self._cluster.release(item.node_id, self.task_index[item.task_id].request)
157	            self._released.add(index)
158	
159	    def _place(self, task: Task, node_id: str, clock: int, preempted: tuple[str, ...]) -> None:
160	        self._cluster.occupy(node_id, task.request)
161	        self._placements.append(Placement(task.id, node_id, clock, clock + task.duration, preempted))
162	        self._waits.append(clock - task.arrival)
163	
164	    # -- run -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
165	    def run(self) -> SimulationResult:
166	        clock = 0
167	        waiting: list[Task] = [task for task in self.tasks if task.arrival == 0]
168	        not_arrived: list[Task] = [task for task in self.tasks if task.arrival > 0]
169	        guard = 0
170	        limit = max(1, len(self.tasks)) * 1000 + 1000
171	
172	        while (waiting or not_arrived or self._active(clock)) and guard < limit:
173	            guard += 1
174	            self._release_finished(clock)
175	            waiting.extend(task for task in list(not_arrived) if task.arrival <= clock)
176	            not_arrived = [task for task in not_arrived if task.arrival > clock]
177	
178	            if not waiting and not self._active(clock) and not_arrived:
179	                clock = min(task.arrival for task in not_arrived)
180	                continue
181	            if not waiting and not self._active(clock):
182	                break
183	
184	            progressed = False
185	            # The head is re-picked after every attempt: a placement (or a preemption inside
186	            # `_try_place`) changes queue shares, so fair mode re-ranks the waiting list each time.
187	            # Without weights the ordering keys never change, which leaves the baseline walk identical.
188	            # A task already refused as head at THIS clock is never refused a second time after one of
189	            # its own backfills (or a fair-share re-rank) tightened the free numbers: the re-check the
190	            # backfill loop performs must not write a duplicate refusal.
191	            refused_at_clock: set[str] = set()
192	            while waiting:
193	                ordered = self._pending_order(waiting, clock)
194	                head = ordered[0]
195	                if head.id not in refused_at_clock:
196	                    if self._try_place(head, clock):
197	                        waiting.remove(head)
198	                        progressed = True
199	                        continue
200	                    refused_at_clock.add(head.id)
201	                # The head cannot be served right now. Conservative backfill looks PAST it -- at the
202	                # tasks behind it in this same deterministic order -- and starts the first one that
203	                # already fits a node and finishes by the earliest running completion, so it cannot
204	                # delay the head it jumped. Nothing may jump when nothing is running (the capacity
205	                # the head waits for cannot reappear before a completion), and --no-backfill forbids
206	                # jumping altogether.
207	                if not self.backfill:
208	                    break
209	                horizon = self._running_end(clock)
210	                if horizon is None:
211	                    break
212	                jumped = False
213	                # The order and horizon are rebuilt after every jump: shares and occupancy changed.
214	                for candidate in self._pending_order(waiting, clock)[1:]:
215	                    if clock + candidate.duration > horizon:
216	                        continue  # past the time boundary: not a placement and not a refusal
217	                    if self._try_backfill(candidate, clock):
218	                        waiting.remove(candidate)
219	                        progressed = True
220	                        jumped = True
221	                        break
222	                    # A failed probe changes nothing: no pseudo-placement, no logged refusal, no
223	                    # preemption. The scan continues with the next candidate in the same order.
224	                if not jumped:
225	                    break  # nobody behind the head qualified this tick
226	
227	            if not self._active(clock) and not not_arrived:
228	                break
229	            candidates = [item.end for item in self._active(clock) if item.end > clock]
230	            candidates += [task.arrival for task in not_arrived if task.arrival > clock]
231	            if not candidates:
232	                break
233	            if progressed and waiting and self._running_end(clock) is not None and not not_arrived:
234	                # capacity is full but something is still waiting: jump straight to the next completion
235	                clock = min(item.end for item in self._active(clock))
236	            else:
237	                clock = min(candidates)
238	
239	        placed_ids = {item.task_id for item in self._placements}
240	        unplaced = sorted(task.id for task in self.tasks if task.id not in placed_ids)
241	        for task in self._pending_order(waiting, clock):
242	            self._decisions.append(
243	                self._annotate(
244	                    {"task": task.id, "reason": "left unplaced when the simulation ended"},
245	                    self._fair_context(task, clock),
246	                )
247	            )
248	        makespan = max((item.end for item in self._placements), default=0)
249	        return SimulationResult(
250	            policy=self.policy,
251	            placements=sorted(self._placements, key=lambda item: (item.start, item.task_id)),
252	            decisions=self._decisions,
253	            unplaced=unplaced,
254	            makespan=makespan,
255	            metrics=self._metrics(makespan, unplaced),
256	        )
257	
258	    def _record_refusal(self, task: Task, reason: str, clock: int, context: dict[str, object] | None = None) -> None:
259	        """Append a refusal only when it differs from the previous one for this task.
260	
261	        The scheduler retries the same blocked task at every tick, so logging each attempt verbatim
262	        repeated one sentence seven times in the trace and buried the decisions that mattered.
263	        """
264	        previous = self._last_refusal.get(task.id)
265	        if previous == reason:
266	            return
267	        self._last_refusal[task.id] = reason
268	        self._decisions.append(
269	            self._annotate({"task": task.id, "reason": reason, "at": clock}, context or self._fair_context(task, clock))
270	        )
271	
272	    def _fair_context(self, task: Task, clock: int) -> dict[str, object]:
273	        """The fair-share fields recorded *before* the decision mutates anything.
274	
275	        Captured at the top of a placement attempt -- after finished tasks were released this tick
276	        but ahead of the occupy or preemption the decision performs -- so a placement records the
277	        share it was actually chosen against.
278	        """
279	        if not self.fair:
280	            return {}
281	        shares = self._shares(clock)
282	        return {
283	            "queue": task.queue,
284	            "weight": self._weight(task.queue),
285	            "weightedDominantShare": round(float(shares.get(task.queue, Fraction(0))), 6),
286	        }
287	
288	    def _annotate(self, document: dict[str, object], context: dict[str, object]) -> dict[str, object]:
289	        document.update(context)
290	        return document
291	
292	    def _try_place(self, task: Task, clock: int) -> bool:
293	        context = self._fair_context(task, clock)
294	        decision = select_node(self._cluster, task, self.policy)
295	        if decision.node_id is not None:
296	            self._place(task, decision.node_id, clock, ())
297	            self._decisions.append(
298	                self._annotate(
299	                    {
300	                        "task": task.id,
301	                        "node": decision.node_id,
302	                        "reason": decision.reason,
303	                        "at": clock,
304	                    },
305	                    context,
306	                )
307	            )
308	            self._last_refusal.pop(task.id, None)
309	            return True
310	        if not self.allow_preemption:
311	            self._record_refusal(task, decision.reason, clock, context)

313	        for node in sorted(self._cluster.nodes, key=lambda item: item.id):

"""Deterministic scheduler simulation: an event clock, conservative backfill, and metrics.

The simulator is a pure function of its input. It never consults the wall clock, never iterates a
`set` in a way that affects a decision, and never breaks a tie by insertion order -- so the same
cluster and task list always produce the same trace, and `replay` proves it instead of asserting it.

One list holds every placement ever made; "running" is derived from the clock (`start <= t < end`),
which removes any chance of the bookkeeping disagreeing with the schedule. Capacity is released
exactly once per placement, tracked by index.

With ``queue_weights`` supplied the run is in fair-share mode: priorities still order the waiting
list, but tasks of equal priority are picked from the queue with the smallest weighted dominant
share -- max(used CPU / total CPU, used memory / total memory) / weight -- and shares are
recomputed after every release, placement and preemption. Shares are kept as exact rational
ratios (``Fraction``), so ordering never loses precision on large integer capacities; the value
is rounded to six decimals only when it leaves the simulator in a trace or metric document.
Without that mapping, nothing changes.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from fractions import Fraction

from .errors import ValidationError
from .model import Cluster, Node, Placement, Resources, Task
from .policies import POLICIES, fragmentation, preemption_candidates, select_node


@dataclass(slots=True)
class SimulationResult:
    policy: str
    placements: list[Placement]
    decisions: list[dict[str, object]]
    unplaced: list[str]
    makespan: int
    metrics: dict[str, object]

    def trace(self) -> list[tuple[str, str, int, int]]:
        """The identity of a run: (task, node, start, end) sorted -- what determinism is checked on."""
        return sorted((item.task_id, item.node_id, item.start, item.end) for item in self.placements)

    def to_document(self) -> dict[str, object]:
        return {
            "policy": self.policy,
            "makespan": self.makespan,
            "placed": len(self.placements),
            "unplaced": self.unplaced,
            "metrics": self.metrics,
            "placements": [item.to_document() for item in self.placements],
        }


@dataclass(slots=True)
class Simulation:
    nodes: tuple[Node, ...]
    tasks: tuple[Task, ...]
    policy: str = "first-fit"
    allow_preemption: bool = False
    backfill: bool = True
    queue_weights: dict[str, int] | None = None
    _cluster: Cluster = field(init=False)
    _placements: list[Placement] = field(default_factory=list, init=False)
    _released: set[int] = field(default_factory=set, init=False)
    _decisions: list[dict[str, object]] = field(default_factory=list, init=False)
    _preemptions: int = field(default=0, init=False)
    _waits: list[int] = field(default_factory=list, init=False)
    _last_refusal: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict, init=False)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.policy not in POLICIES:
            raise ValidationError(f"policy must be one of {', '.join(POLICIES)}", value=self.policy)
        ids = [task.id for task in self.tasks]
        if len(set(ids)) != len(ids):
            raise ValidationError("task ids must be unique")
        if self.queue_weights is not None:
            if not self.queue_weights:
                raise ValidationError("queue weights must declare at least one queue")
            for name, weight in self.queue_weights.items():
                if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
                    raise ValidationError("queue weights must use non-empty queue names", value=name)
                if isinstance(weight, bool) or not isinstance(weight, int) or weight <= 0:
                    raise ValidationError("queue weights must be positive integers", queue=name, value=weight)
        self._cluster = Cluster(self.nodes)

    # -- bookkeeping -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
    @property
    def task_index(self) -> dict[str, Task]:
        return {task.id: task for task in self.tasks}

    @property
    def fair(self) -> bool:
        return self.queue_weights is not None

    def _weight(self, queue: str) -> int:
        # A queue used by a task but absent from the config carries an implicit weight of one.
        assert self.queue_weights is not None
        return self.queue_weights.get(queue, 1)

    def _shares(self, clock: int) -> dict[str, Fraction]:
        """Weighted dominant share of every queue from the tasks running at ``clock``.

        The dominant resource is the larger of the queue's CPU and memory fractions of total cluster
        capacity; dividing by the queue weight yields its weighted dominant share. Shares are exact
        rational ratios built from the integer inputs, so two shares that differ by less than one
        binary floating-point ulp still order correctly -- the ratio is rounded to six decimals only
        when it is written into a trace or metric document. A resource with zero total capacity
        contributes a zero fraction (never a division by zero).
        """
        assert self.queue_weights is not None
        running = self._active(clock)
        used: dict[str, Resources] = {}
        for item in running:
            task = self.task_index[item.task_id]
            used[task.queue] = used.get(task.queue, Resources(0, 0)).plus(task.request)
        capacity = self._cluster.total_capacity()
        shares: dict[str, Fraction] = {}
        for queue, request in used.items():
            cpu_fraction = Fraction(request.cpu, capacity.cpu) if capacity.cpu else Fraction(0)
            memory_fraction = Fraction(request.memory, capacity.memory) if capacity.memory else Fraction(0)
            shares[queue] = max(cpu_fraction, memory_fraction) / self._weight(queue)
        return shares

    def _pending_order(self, pending: list[Task], clock: int) -> list[Task]:
        if not self.fair:
            return sorted(pending, key=lambda task: (-task.priority, task.arrival, task.id))
        shares = self._shares(clock)
        return sorted(
            pending,
            key=lambda task: (
                -task.priority,
                shares.get(task.queue, Fraction(0)),
                task.arrival,
                task.queue,
                task.id,
            ),
        )

    def _active(self, clock: int) -> list[Placement]:
        return [item for item in self._placements if item.start <= clock < item.end]

    def _running_end(self, clock: int) -> int | None:
        ends = [item.end for item in self._active(clock)]
        return min(ends) if ends else None

    def _release_finished(self, clock: int) -> None:
        """Free capacity for everything that has ended by `clock`, once per placement.

        This runs *before* placement at the same tick: capacity freed at t must be available to the
        task considered at t. The first version placed first and released afterwards, which held
        resources one tick too long.
        """
        for index, item in enumerate(self._placements):
            if index in self._released or item.end > clock:
                continue
            self._cluster.release(item.node_id, self.task_index[item.task_id].request)
            self._released.add(index)

    def _place(self, task: Task, node_id: str, clock: int, preempted: tuple[str, ...]) -> None:
        self._cluster.occupy(node_id, task.request)
        self._placements.append(Placement(task.id, node_id, clock, clock + task.duration, preempted))
        self._waits.append(clock - task.arrival)

    # -- run -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def run(self) -> SimulationResult:
        clock = 0
        waiting: list[Task] = [task for task in self.tasks if task.arrival == 0]
        not_arrived: list[Task] = [task for task in self.tasks if task.arrival > 0]
        guard = 0
        limit = max(1, len(self.tasks)) * 1000 + 1000

        while (waiting or not_arrived or self._active(clock)) and guard < limit:
            guard += 1
            self._release_finished(clock)
            waiting.extend(task for task in list(not_arrived) if task.arrival <= clock)
            not_arrived = [task for task in not_arrived if task.arrival > clock]

            if not waiting and not self._active(clock) and not_arrived:
                clock = min(task.arrival for task in not_arrived)
                continue
            if not waiting and not self._active(clock):
                break

            progressed = False
            # The head is re-picked after every attempt: a placement (or a preemption inside
            # `_try_place`) changes queue shares, so fair mode re-ranks the waiting list each time.
            # Without weights the ordering keys never change, which leaves the baseline walk identical.
            # A task already refused as head at THIS clock is never refused a second time after one of
            # its own backfills (or a fair-share re-rank) tightened the free numbers: the re-check the
            # backfill loop performs must not write a duplicate refusal.
            refused_at_clock: set[str] = set()
            while waiting:
                ordered = self._pending_order(waiting, clock)
                head = ordered[0]
                if head.id not in refused_at_clock:
                    if self._try_place(head, clock):
                        waiting.remove(head)
                        progressed = True
                        continue
                    refused_at_clock.add(head.id)
                # The head cannot be served right now. Conservative backfill looks PAST it -- at the
                # tasks behind it in this same deterministic order -- and starts the first one that
                # already fits a node and finishes by the earliest running completion, so it cannot
                # delay the head it jumped. Nothing may jump when nothing is running (the capacity
                # the head waits for cannot reappear before a completion), and --no-backfill forbids
                # jumping altogether.
                if not self.backfill:
                    break
                horizon = self._running_end(clock)
                if horizon is None:
                    break
                jumped = False
                # The order and horizon are rebuilt after every jump: shares and occupancy changed.
                for candidate in self._pending_order(waiting, clock)[1:]:
                    if clock + candidate.duration > horizon:
                        continue  # past the time boundary: not a placement and not a refusal
                    if self._try_backfill(candidate, clock):
                        waiting.remove(candidate)
                        progressed = True
                        jumped = True
                        break
                    # A failed probe changes nothing: no pseudo-placement, no logged refusal, no
                    # preemption. The scan continues with the next candidate in the same order.
                if not jumped:
                    break  # nobody behind the head qualified this tick

            if not self._active(clock) and not not_arrived:
                break
            candidates = [item.end for item in self._active(clock) if item.end > clock]
            candidates += [task.arrival for task in not_arrived if task.arrival > clock]
            if not candidates:
                break
            if progressed and waiting and self._running_end(clock) is not None and not not_arrived:
                # capacity is full but something is still waiting: jump straight to the next completion
                clock = min(item.end for item in self._active(clock))
            else:
                clock = min(candidates)

        placed_ids = {item.task_id for item in self._placements}
        unplaced = sorted(task.id for task in self.tasks if task.id not in placed_ids)
        for task in self._pending_order(waiting, clock):
            self._decisions.append(
                self._annotate(
                    {"task": task.id, "reason": "left unplaced when the simulation ended"},
                    self._fair_context(task, clock),
                )
            )
        makespan = max((item.end for item in self._placements), default=0)
        return SimulationResult(
            policy=self.policy,
            placements=sorted(self._placements, key=lambda item: (item.start, item.task_id)),
            decisions=self._decisions,
            unplaced=unplaced,
            makespan=makespan,
            metrics=self._metrics(makespan, unplaced),
        )

    def _record_refusal(self, task: Task, reason: str, clock: int, context: dict[str, object] | None = None) -> None:
        """Append a refusal only when it differs from the previous one for this task.

        The scheduler retries the same blocked task at every tick, so logging each attempt verbatim
        repeated one sentence seven times in the trace and buried the decisions that mattered.
        """
        previous = self._last_refusal.get(task.id)
        if previous == reason:
            return
        self._last_refusal[task.id] = reason
        self._decisions.append(
            self._annotate({"task": task.id, "reason": reason, "at": clock}, context or self._fair_context(task, clock))
        )

    def _fair_context(self, task: Task, clock: int) -> dict[str, object]:
        """The fair-share fields recorded *before* the decision mutates anything.

        Captured at the top of a placement attempt -- after finished tasks were released this tick
        but ahead of the occupy or preemption the decision performs -- so a placement records the
        share it was actually chosen against.
        """
        if not self.fair:
            return {}
        shares = self._shares(clock)
        return {
            "queue": task.queue,
            "weight": self._weight(task.queue),
            "weightedDominantShare": round(float(shares.get(task.queue, Fraction(0))), 6),
        }

    def _annotate(self, document: dict[str, object], context: dict[str, object]) -> dict[str, object]:
        document.update(context)
        return document

    def _try_place(self, task: Task, clock: int) -> bool:
        context = self._fair_context(task, clock)
        decision = select_node(self._cluster, task, self.policy)
        if decision.node_id is not None:
            self._place(task, decision.node_id, clock, ())
            self._decisions.append(
                self._annotate(
                    {
                        "task": task.id,
                        "node": decision.node_id,
                        "reason": decision.reason,
                        "at": clock,
                    },
                    context,
                )
            )
            self._last_refusal.pop(task.id, None)
            return True
        if not self.allow_preemption:
            self._record_refusal(task, decision.reason, clock, context)
            return False
        for node in sorted(self._cluster.nodes, key=lambda item: item.id):
            chosen, reason = preemption_candidates(self._cluster, task, node, self._placements, self.task_index, clock)
            if not chosen:
                continue
            for item in chosen:
                index = self._placements.index(item)
                self._cluster.release(item.node_id, self.task_index[item.task_id].request)
                self._placements[index] = Placement(item.task_id, item.node_id, item.start, clock, item.preempted)
                self._released.add(index)
                self._preemptions += 1
            self._place(task, node.id, clock, tuple(sorted(item.task_id for item in chosen)))
            self._decisions.append(
                self._annotate({"task": task.id, "node": node.id, "reason": reason, "at": clock}, context)
            )
            self._last_refusal.pop(task.id, None)
            return True
        self._record_refusal(task, decision.reason, clock, context)
        return False

    def _try_backfill(self, task: Task, clock: int) -> bool:
        """Place a task jumping a blocked head, or fail with NO side effects.

        The caller has already checked the time boundary (``clock + duration`` must not pass the
        earliest running completion). The probe applies exactly the same node selection as a normal
        attempt -- capacity, affinity, anti-affinity, taints and the first-fit / best-fit node order
        are unchanged. A candidate that does not fit right now produces neither a placement nor a
        refusal and never triggers preemption: probing is free and invisible, so a failed candidate
        can still be placed later as an ordinary head.
        """
        decision = select_node(self._cluster, task, self.policy)
        if decision.node_id is None:
            return False
        context = self._fair_context(task, clock)
        self._place(task, decision.node_id, clock, ())
        self._decisions.append(
            self._annotate(
                {
                    "task": task.id,
                    "node": decision.node_id,
                    "reason": "backfill",
                    "at": clock,
                },
                context,
            )
        )
        self._last_refusal.pop(task.id, None)
        return True

    def _metrics(self, makespan: int, unplaced: list[str]) -> dict[str, object]:
        total_cpu = self._cluster.total_capacity().cpu
        used_cpu_time = sum(self.task_index[item.task_id].request.cpu * (item.end - item.start) for item in self._placements)
        metrics: dict[str, object] = {
            "makespan": makespan,
            "placed": len(self._placements),
            "unplaced": len(unplaced),
            "preemptions": self._preemptions,
            "averageWait": round(sum(self._waits) / len(self._waits), 3) if self._waits else 0.0,
            "maxWait": max(self._waits) if self._waits else 0,
            "utilization": round(used_cpu_time / (total_cpu * makespan), 6) if total_cpu and makespan else 0.0,
            "fragmentation": fragmentation(self._cluster, {task.id: task for task in self.tasks if task.id in set(unplaced)}),
        }
        if self.fair:
            metrics["queues"] = self._queue_metrics(makespan, set(unplaced))
        return metrics

    def _queue_metrics(self, makespan: int, unplaced: set[str]) -> dict[str, object]:
        """Per-queue accounting over the actual run intervals.

        Resource time is summed over each placement's real ``[start, end)`` interval, so a preempted
        task counts only up to the tick it was evicted. The dominant share integrates the same
        intervals over the whole makespan: max(cpu-time/capacity, memory-time/memory) / makespan /
        weight. Zero capacity or zero makespan yields zero.
        """
        assert self.queue_weights is not None
        names = {task.queue for task in self.tasks}
        cpu_capacity = self._cluster.total_capacity().cpu
        memory_capacity = self._cluster.total_capacity().memory
        cpu_time: dict[str, int] = {}
        memory_time: dict[str, int] = {}
        waits: dict[str, list[int]] = {}
        for item in self._placements:
            task = self.task_index[item.task_id]
            duration = item.end - item.start
            cpu_time[task.queue] = cpu_time.get(task.queue, 0) + task.request.cpu * duration
            memory_time[task.queue] = memory_time.get(task.queue, 0) + task.request.memory * duration
            waits.setdefault(task.queue, []).append(item.start - task.arrival)
        report: dict[str, object] = {}
        for name in sorted(names):
            queue_waits = waits.get(name, [])
            cpu_share = cpu_time.get(name, 0) / (cpu_capacity * makespan) if cpu_capacity and makespan else 0.0
            memory_share = memory_time.get(name, 0) / (memory_capacity * makespan) if memory_capacity and makespan else 0.0
            report[name] = {
                "weight": self._weight(name),
                "placed": len(queue_waits),
                "unplaced": sum(1 for task in self.tasks if task.queue == name and task.id in unplaced),
                "averageWait": round(sum(queue_waits) / len(queue_waits), 3) if queue_waits else 0.0,
                "cpuTime": cpu_time.get(name, 0),
                "memoryTime": memory_time.get(name, 0),
                "dominantShare": round(max(cpu_share, memory_share) / self._weight(name), 6),
            }
        return report


def simulate(nodes: tuple[Node, ...], tasks: tuple[Task, ...], **options: object) -> SimulationResult:
    return Simulation(nodes=nodes, tasks=tasks, **options).run()  # type: ignore[arg-type]


def replay(nodes: tuple[Node, ...], tasks: tuple[Task, ...], **options: object) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Run twice and compare the traces: the determinism guarantee, checked rather than asserted."""
    first = simulate(nodes, tasks, **options)
    second = simulate(nodes, tasks, **options)
    identical = first.trace() == second.trace()
    return {
        "identical": identical,
        "policy": first.policy,
        "placements": len(first.placements),
        "makespan": first.makespan,
        "trace": [list(item) for item in first.trace()][:20],
        "differences": [] if identical else [list(item) for item in first.trace() if item not in second.trace()][:20],
    }


def compare_policies(
    nodes: tuple[Node, ...],
    tasks: tuple[Task, ...],
    policies: tuple[str, ...] = POLICIES,
    **options: object,
) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Same cluster, same tasks, different placement policies: metrics side by side."""
    results: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    for policy in policies:
        result = simulate(nodes, tasks, policy=policy, **options)
        entry: dict[str, object] = {
            "policy": policy,
            "makespan": result.makespan,
            "placed": len(result.placements),
            "unplaced": len(result.unplaced),
            "averageWait": result.metrics["averageWait"],
            "utilization": result.metrics["utilization"],
        }
        if "queues" in result.metrics:
            entry["queues"] = result.metrics["queues"]
        results.append(entry)
    return {"policies": results}

1	"""Command line entry point.
2	
3	A cluster is a JSONL node list; a task set is a JSONL task list. Both are validated with line numbers,
4	so a bad request says exactly where it went wrong. Every subcommand writes one JSON document to stdout;
5	errors are one JSON document on stderr. Exit codes: 0 success, 2 input/usage error, 3 a report whose
6	verdict is negative (tasks left unplaced, or two runs that disagreed).
7	"""
8	
9	from __future__ import annotations
10	
11	import argparse
12	import json
13	import sys
14	from typing import Any, Sequence
15	
16	from . import __version__
17	from .errors import ParseError, SchedulerError, ValidationError
18	from .model import Node, Resources, Task
19	from .policies import POLICIES
20	from .simulator import Simulation, compare_policies, replay, simulate
21	
22	EXIT_OK = 0
23	EXIT_ERROR = 2
24	EXIT_NEGATIVE = 3
25	
26	
27	def canonical(document: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
28	    return json.dumps(document, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)
29	
30	
31	def _emit(document: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
32	    sys.stdout.write(canonical(document) + "\n")
33	
34	
35	def _read_lines(path: str) -> list[str]:
36	    if path == "-":
37	        return sys.stdin.read().splitlines()
38	    try:
39	        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
40	            return handle.read().splitlines()
41	    except OSError as error:
42	        raise ValidationError(f"cannot read input: {error.strerror or error}", value=path) from error
43	
44	
45	def _rows(path: str, what: str) -> list[tuple[int, dict[str, Any]]]:
46	    rows: list[tuple[int, dict[str, Any]]] = []
47	    for number, text in enumerate(_read_lines(path), start=1):
48	        stripped = text.strip()
49	        if not stripped or stripped.startswith("#"):
50	            continue
51	        try:
52	            document = json.loads(stripped)
53	        except json.JSONDecodeError as error:
54	            raise ParseError(f"{what} line {number}: invalid JSON: {error.msg}", line=number) from error
55	        if not isinstance(document, dict):
56	            raise ParseError(f"{what} line {number}: expected a JSON object", line=number)
57	        rows.append((number, document))
58	    return rows
59	
60	
61	def _pairs(document: dict[str, Any], key: str, number: int, what: str) -> tuple[tuple[str, str], ...]:
62	    value = document.get(key, {})
63	    if value in (None, {}):
64	        return ()
65	    if not isinstance(value, dict):
66	        raise ParseError(f"{what} line {number}: {key} must be an object", line=number)
67	    return tuple(sorted((str(item), str(target)) for item, target in value.items()))
68	
69	
70	def _strings(document: dict[str, Any], key: str, number: int, what: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:
71	    value = document.get(key, [])
72	    if value in (None, []):
73	        return ()
74	    if not isinstance(value, list) or any(not isinstance(item, str) for item in value):
75	        raise ParseError(f"{what} line {number}: {key} must be a list of strings", line=number)
76	    return tuple(sorted(str(item) for item in value))
77	
78	
79	def _resources(document: dict[str, Any], number: int, what: str) -> Resources:
80	    cpu = document.get("cpu", 0)
81	    memory = document.get("memory", 0)
82	    for name, value in (("cpu", cpu), ("memory", memory)):
83	        if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int):
84	            raise ParseError(f"{what} line {number}: {name} must be an integer", line=number)
85	    return Resources(cpu, memory)
86	
87	
88	def load_cluster(path: str) -> tuple[Node, ...]:
89	    nodes: list[Node] = []
90	    for number, document in _rows(path, "cluster"):
91	        unknown = sorted(set(document) - {"id", "cpu", "memory", "labels", "taints"})
92	        if unknown:
93	            raise ParseError(f"cluster line {number}: unknown field(s): {', '.join(unknown)}", line=number)
94	        if "id" not in document:
95	            raise ParseError(f"cluster line {number}: missing id", line=number)
96	        nodes.append(
97	            Node(
98	                id=str(document["id"]),
99	                capacity=_resources(document, number, "cluster"),
100	                labels=_pairs(document, "labels", number, "cluster"),
101	                taints=_strings(document, "taints", number, "cluster"),
102	            )
103	        )
104	    if not nodes:
105	        raise ValidationError("the cluster is empty")
106	    return tuple(nodes)
107	
108	
109	def load_tasks(path: str) -> tuple[Task, ...]:
110	    tasks: list[Task] = []
111	    known = {"id", "cpu", "memory", "priority", "queue", "arrival", "duration", "affinity", "antiAffinity", "tolerations"}
112	    for number, document in _rows(path, "task"):
113	        unknown = sorted(set(document) - known)
114	        if unknown:
115	            raise ParseError(f"task line {number}: unknown field(s): {', '.join(unknown)}", line=number)
116	        if "id" not in document:
117	            raise ParseError(f"task line {number}: missing id", line=number)
118	        for name in ("priority", "arrival", "duration"):
119	            value = document.get(name)
120	            if value is not None and (isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int)):
121	                raise ParseError(f"task line {number}: {name} must be an integer", line=number)
122	        tasks.append(
123	            Task(
124	                id=str(document["id"]),
125	                request=_resources(document, number, "task"),
126	                priority=int(document.get("priority", 0)),
127	                queue=str(document.get("queue", "default")),
128	                arrival=int(document.get("arrival", 0)),
129	                duration=int(document.get("duration", 1)),
130	                affinity=_pairs(document, "affinity", number, "task"),
131	                anti_affinity=_strings(document, "antiAffinity", number, "task"),
132	                tolerations=_strings(document, "tolerations", number, "task"),
133	            )
134	        )
135	    if not tasks:
136	        raise ValidationError("the task set is empty")
137	    return tuple(tasks)
138	
139	
140	def load_queue_weights(path: str) -> dict[str, int]:
141	    """Parse the optional JSONL ``{"queue": ..., "weight": ...}`` file.
142	
143	    Shape problems -- broken JSON, a non-object row, missing fields, wrong types, unknown fields --
144	    are parse errors naming the raw line. Semantic problems -- a non-positive weight or a queue
145	    declared twice -- are validation errors. A file with no valid rows is rejected rather than
146	    silently treated as "no config" (which would run the baseline instead of the requested mode).
147	    """
148	    weights: dict[str, int] = {}
149	    for number, document in _rows(path, "queue weights"):
150	        unknown = sorted(set(document) - {"queue", "weight"})
151	        if unknown:
152	            raise ParseError(f"queue weights line {number}: unknown field(s): {', '.join(unknown)}", line=number)
153	        if "queue" not in document:
154	            raise ParseError(f"queue weights line {number}: missing queue", line=number)
155	        if "weight" not in document:
156	            raise ParseError(f"queue weights line {number}: missing weight", line=number)
157	        queue = document["queue"]
158	        weight = document["weight"]
159	        if not isinstance(queue, str) or not queue:
160	            raise ParseError(f"queue weights line {number}: queue must be a non-empty string", line=number)
161	        if isinstance(weight, bool) or not isinstance(weight, int):
162	            raise ParseError(f"queue weights line {number}: weight must be an integer", line=number)
163	        if weight <= 0:
164	            raise ValidationError(
165	                f"queue weights line {number}: weight must be positive", line=number, queue=queue, value=weight
166	            )
167	        if queue in weights:
168	            raise ValidationError(
169	                f"queue weights line {number}: duplicate queue {queue!r}", line=number, queue=queue
170	            )
171	        weights[queue] = weight
172	    if not weights:
173	        raise ValidationError("the queue weights file is empty", value=path)
174	    return weights
175	
176	
177	def _options(args: argparse.Namespace) -> dict[str, object]:
178	    options: dict[str, object] = {
179	        "policy": args.policy,
180	        "allow_preemption": args.preemption,
181	        "backfill": not args.no_backfill,
182	    }
183	    path = getattr(args, "queue_weights", None)
184	    if path:
185	        options["queue_weights"] = load_queue_weights(path)
186	    return options
187	
188	
189	# -- commands ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
190	def _command_describe(_: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
191	    _emit(
192	        {
193	            "name": "cluster-scheduler-simulator",
194	            "version": __version__,
195	            "subcommands": ["describe", "metrics", "policies", "replay", "simulate", "trace", "validate"],
196	            "policies": list(POLICIES),
197	            "clusterFields": ["id", "cpu", "memory", "labels", "taints"],
198	            "taskFields": [
199	                "id",
200	                "cpu",
201	                "memory",
202	                "priority",
203	                "queue",
204	                "arrival",
205	                "duration",
206	                "affinity",
207	                "antiAffinity",
208	                "tolerations",
209	            ],
210	            "deterministic": "no wall clock, no set iteration, ties always break on id",
211	            "exitCodes": {"ok": EXIT_OK, "error": EXIT_ERROR, "negativeVerdict": EXIT_NEGATIVE},
212	        }
213	    )
214	    return EXIT_OK
215	
216	
217	def _command_validate(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
218	    nodes = load_cluster(args.cluster)
219	    tasks = load_tasks(args.tasks)
220	    # Constructing the simulation *is* the validation: `Cluster` catches duplicate node ids and
221	    # `Simulation` catches duplicate task ids. It takes no options on purpose -- `validate` checks the
222	    # inputs, and the policy is already constrained by argparse. (Reading `_options(args)` here crashed:
223	    # the validate subparser has no policy flags, which the test suite caught immediately.)
224	    Simulation(nodes=nodes, tasks=tasks)
225	    _emit(
226	        {
227	            "nodes": len(nodes),
228	            "tasks": len(tasks),
229	            "totalCapacity": _total_capacity(nodes),
230	            "requested": _total_requested(tasks),
231	        }
232	    )
233	    return EXIT_OK
234	
235	
236	def _total_capacity(nodes: tuple[Node, ...]) -> dict[str, int]:
237	    cpu = sum(node.capacity.cpu for node in nodes)
238	    memory = sum(node.capacity.memory for node in nodes)
239	    return {"cpu": cpu, "memory": memory}
240	
241	
242	def _total_requested(tasks: tuple[Task, ...]) -> dict[str, int]:
243	    cpu = sum(task.request.cpu for task in tasks)
244	    memory = sum(task.request.memory for task in tasks)
245	    return {"cpu": cpu, "memory": memory}
246	
247	
248	def _command_simulate(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
249	    result = simulate(load_cluster(args.cluster), load_tasks(args.tasks), **_options(args))
250	    _emit(result.to_document())
251	    return EXIT_OK if not result.unplaced else EXIT_NEGATIVE
252	
253	
254	def _command_trace(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
255	    result = simulate(load_cluster(args.cluster), load_tasks(args.tasks), **_options(args))
256	    _emit(
257	        {
258	            "policy": result.policy,
259	            "makespan": result.makespan,
260	            "decisions": result.decisions,
261	            "unplaced": result.unplaced,
262	        }
263	    )
264	    return EXIT_OK if not result.unplaced else EXIT_NEGATIVE
265	
266	
267	def _command_metrics(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
268	    result = simulate(load_cluster(args.cluster), load_tasks(args.tasks), **_options(args))
269	    _emit({"policy": result.policy, "metrics": result.metrics})
270	    return EXIT_OK if not result.unplaced else EXIT_NEGATIVE
271	
272	
273	def _command_policies(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
274	    report = compare_policies(load_cluster(args.cluster), load_tasks(args.tasks), **{k: v for k, v in _options(args).items() if k != "policy"})
275	    _emit(report)
276	    best = min(report["policies"], key=lambda entry: (entry["unplaced"], entry["makespan"], entry["policy"]))
277	    return EXIT_OK if best["unplaced"] == 0 else EXIT_NEGATIVE
278	
279	
280	def _command_replay(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
281	    report = replay(load_cluster(args.cluster), load_tasks(args.tasks), **_options(args))
282	    _emit(report)
283	    return EXIT_OK if report["identical"] else EXIT_NEGATIVE
284	
285	
286	def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
287	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="cluster-scheduler-simulator", description="deterministic cluster scheduling simulation")
288	    parser.add_argument("--version", action="version", version=f"cluster-scheduler-simulator {__version__}")
289	    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
290	
291	    subparsers.add_parser("describe", help="print capabilities as JSON").set_defaults(handler=_command_describe)
292	
293	    def with_inputs(name: str, help_text: str) -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
294	        sub = subparsers.add_parser(name, help=help_text)
295	        sub.add_argument("--cluster", required=True, help="JSONL nodes, or - for stdin")
296	        sub.add_argument("--tasks", required=True, help="JSONL tasks")
297	        return sub
298	
299	    def with_options(sub: argparse.ArgumentParser) -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
300	        sub.add_argument("--policy", choices=list(POLICIES), default="first-fit")
301	        sub.add_argument("--preemption", action="store_true", help="allow higher priorities to evict lower ones")
302	        sub.add_argument("--no-backfill", action="store_true", help="disable conservative backfill")
303	        sub.add_argument(
304	            "--queue-weights",
305	            metavar="PATH",
306	            help="JSONL {queue, weight} rows; enables weighted fair-share scheduling",
307	        )
308	        return sub
309	
310	    with_inputs("validate", "parse and validate both inputs").set_defaults(handler=_command_validate)
311	    with_options(with_inputs("simulate", "run the simulation")).set_defaults(handler=_command_simulate)
312	    with_options(with_inputs("trace", "per-decision scheduling trace")).set_defaults(handler=_command_trace)
313	    with_options(with_inputs("metrics", "metrics only")).set_defaults(handler=_command_metrics)
314	    with_options(with_inputs("replay", "run twice and check the traces match")).set_defaults(handler=_command_replay)
315	    with_options(with_inputs("policies", "compare first-fit and best-fit")).set_defaults(handler=_command_policies)
316	    return parser
317	
318	
319	def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
320	    parser = build_parser()
321	    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
322	    try:
323	        return int(args.handler(args))
324	    except SchedulerError as error:
325	        sys.stderr.write(canonical(error.to_document()) + "\n")
326	        return EXIT_ERROR
327	
328	
329	if __name__ == "__main__":  # pragma: no cover
330	    raise SystemExit(main())

3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	import contextlib
6	import io
7	import json
8	import os
9	import tempfile
10	import unittest
11	
12	from schedsim.cli import EXIT_ERROR, EXIT_NEGATIVE, EXIT_OK, main
13	
14	CLUSTER = [
15	    {"id": "n1", "cpu": 4, "memory": 8, "labels": {"zone": "a"}},
16	    {"id": "n2", "cpu": 4, "memory": 8, "labels": {"zone": "b"}},
17	]
18	
19	TASKS = [
20	    {"id": "t1", "cpu": 2, "memory": 2, "priority": 1, "duration": 4},
21	    {"id": "t2", "cpu": 2, "memory": 2, "priority": 1, "duration": 2},
22	    {"id": "t3", "cpu": 9, "memory": 9, "priority": 1, "duration": 1},
23	]
24	
25	
26	def run_cli(argv: list[str]) -> tuple[int, str, str]:
27	    out, err = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()
28	    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out), contextlib.redirect_stderr(err):
29	        code = main(argv)
30	    return code, out.getvalue(), err.getvalue()
31

33	class CLITests(unittest.TestCase):
34	    def setUp(self) -> None:
35	        self.directory = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
36	        self.cluster = self.write("cluster.jsonl", CLUSTER)
37	        self.tasks = self.write("tasks.jsonl", TASKS)
38	
39	    def tearDown(self) -> None:
40	        self.directory.cleanup()
41	
42	    def write(self, name: str, rows: list[dict]) -> str:
43	        path = os.path.join(self.directory.name, name)
44	        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as handle:
45	            for row in rows:
46	                handle.write(json.dumps(row) + "\n")
47	        return path
48	
49	    def test_describe_publishes_the_contract(self) -> None:
50	        code, out, err = run_cli(["describe"])
51	        self.assertEqual((code, err), (EXIT_OK, ""))
52	        document = json.loads(out)
53	        self.assertEqual(document["exitCodes"], {"ok": 0, "error": 2, "negativeVerdict": 3})
54	        self.assertEqual(document["policies"], ["first-fit", "best-fit"])

56	    def test_validate_totals_capacity_and_request(self) -> None:
57	        code, out, _ = run_cli(["validate", "--cluster", self.cluster, "--tasks", self.tasks])
58	        self.assertEqual(code, EXIT_OK)
59	        document = json.loads(out)
60	        self.assertEqual(document["totalCapacity"], {"cpu": 8, "memory": 16})
61	        self.assertEqual(document["nodes"], 2)

65	        self.assertEqual(code, EXIT_NEGATIVE)

71	        code, out, _ = run_cli(["simulate", "--cluster", self.cluster, "--tasks", small])

"""CLI contract: JSON on stdout, documented exit codes, and the determinism report."""

from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
import io
import json
import os
import tempfile
import unittest

from schedsim.cli import EXIT_ERROR, EXIT_NEGATIVE, EXIT_OK, main

CLUSTER = [
    {"id": "n1", "cpu": 4, "memory": 8, "labels": {"zone": "a"}},
    {"id": "n2", "cpu": 4, "memory": 8, "labels": {"zone": "b"}},
]

TASKS = [
    {"id": "t1", "cpu": 2, "memory": 2, "priority": 1, "duration": 4},
    {"id": "t2", "cpu": 2, "memory": 2, "priority": 1, "duration": 2},
    {"id": "t3", "cpu": 9, "memory": 9, "priority": 1, "duration": 1},
]


def run_cli(argv: list[str]) -> tuple[int, str, str]:
    out, err = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out), contextlib.redirect_stderr(err):
        code = main(argv)
    return code, out.getvalue(), err.getvalue()


class CLITests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.directory = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.cluster = self.write("cluster.jsonl", CLUSTER)
        self.tasks = self.write("tasks.jsonl", TASKS)

    def tearDown(self) -> None:
        self.directory.cleanup()

    def write(self, name: str, rows: list[dict]) -> str:
        path = os.path.join(self.directory.name, name)
        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as handle:
            for row in rows:
                handle.write(json.dumps(row) + "\n")
        return path

    def test_describe_publishes_the_contract(self) -> None:
        code, out, err = run_cli(["describe"])
        self.assertEqual((code, err), (EXIT_OK, ""))
        document = json.loads(out)
        self.assertEqual(document["exitCodes"], {"ok": 0, "error": 2, "negativeVerdict": 3})
        self.assertEqual(document["policies"], ["first-fit", "best-fit"])

    def test_validate_totals_capacity_and_request(self) -> None:
        code, out, _ = run_cli(["validate", "--cluster", self.cluster, "--tasks", self.tasks])
        self.assertEqual(code, EXIT_OK)
        document = json.loads(out)
        self.assertEqual(document["totalCapacity"], {"cpu": 8, "memory": 16})
        self.assertEqual(document["nodes"], 2)

    def test_simulate_reports_unplaced_as_a_negative_verdict(self) -> None:
        code, out, _ = run_cli(["simulate", "--cluster", self.cluster, "--tasks", self.tasks])
        self.assertEqual(code, EXIT_NEGATIVE)
        document = json.loads(out)
        self.assertEqual(document["unplaced"], ["t3"])

    def test_simulate_full_placement_is_ok(self) -> None:
        small = self.write("small.jsonl", [{"id": "a", "cpu": 1, "memory": 1, "duration": 1}])
        code, out, _ = run_cli(["simulate", "--cluster", self.cluster, "--tasks", small])
        self.assertEqual(code, EXIT_OK)
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(out)["metrics"]["placed"], 1)

    def test_trace_explains_each_decision(self) -> None:
        small = self.write("trace.jsonl", [{"id": "a", "cpu": 1, "memory": 1}, {"id": "b", "cpu": 9}])
        code, out, _ = run_cli(["trace", "--cluster", self.cluster, "--tasks", small])
        self.assertEqual(code, EXIT_NEGATIVE)
        document = json.loads(out)
        reasons = [entry["reason"] for entry in document["decisions"]]
        self.assertTrue(any("placed by first-fit" in reason for reason in reasons))
        self.assertTrue(any("insufficient capacity" in reason for reason in reasons))

    def test_metrics_only(self) -> None:
        small = self.write("m.jsonl", [{"id": "a", "cpu": 4, "memory": 8, "duration": 2}])
        code, out, _ = run_cli(["metrics", "--cluster", self.cluster, "--tasks", small])
        self.assertEqual(code, EXIT_OK)
        metrics = json.loads(out)["metrics"]
        self.assertEqual(metrics["makespan"], 2)
        self.assertGreater(metrics["utilization"], 0.0)

    def test_replay_reports_identical_traces(self) -> None:
        small = self.write("r.jsonl", [{"id": "a", "cpu": 1, "memory": 1}, {"id": "b", "cpu": 2, "memory": 2}])
        code, out, _ = run_cli(["replay", "--cluster", self.cluster, "--tasks", small, "--policy", "best-fit"])
        self.assertEqual(code, EXIT_OK)
        document = json.loads(out)
        self.assertTrue(document["identical"])
        self.assertEqual(document["differences"], [])

    def test_big_integer_inputs_order_by_exact_share_everywhere(self) -> None:
        # 1e20 capacity: queue Z's anchor holds one unit fewer than A's, a difference no binary
        # double can represent at 0.5. The exact ordering must serve z1 before a1 through every
        # public entry point, while the displayed share stays the rounded float 0.5.
        big = 10**20
        half = big // 2
        cluster = self.write(
            "big_cluster.jsonl", [{"id": "n1", "cpu": big, "memory": big}]
        )
        rows = [
            {"id": "aRun", "cpu": half - 2, "memory": 1, "queue": "A", "duration": 10},
            {"id": "zRun", "cpu": half - 3, "memory": 1, "queue": "Z", "duration": 10},
            {"id": "z1", "cpu": 1, "queue": "Z", "arrival": 1},
            {"id": "a1", "cpu": 1, "queue": "A", "arrival": 1},
            {"id": "z2", "cpu": 1, "queue": "Z", "arrival": 1},
            {"id": "a2", "cpu": 1, "queue": "A", "arrival": 1},
        ]
        tasks = self.write("big_tasks.jsonl", rows)
        weights = self.write_weights(
            [{"queue": "A", "weight": 1}, {"queue": "Z", "weight": 1}], "big_weights.jsonl"
        )
        # simulate: every task is placed; placement documents are sorted by (start, task id), so
        # the scheduling order itself is asserted through `trace` below.
        code, out, err = run_cli(["simulate", "--cluster", cluster, "--tasks", tasks, "--queue-weights", weights])
        self.assertEqual((code, err), (EXIT_OK, ""))
        document = json.loads(out)
        self.assertEqual(document["unplaced"], [])
        self.assertEqual([p["task"] for p in document["placements"] if p["start"] == 1], ["a1", "a2", "z1", "z2"])

        # trace: decisions carry a six-decimal float that displays identically for both queues
        code, out, _ = run_cli(["trace", "--cluster", cluster, "--tasks", tasks, "--queue-weights", weights])
        self.assertEqual(code, EXIT_OK)
        decisions = json.loads(out)["decisions"]
        self.assertEqual([d["task"] for d in decisions if d.get("at") == 1 and "node" in d], ["z1", "a1", "z2", "a2"])
        for decision in decisions:
            if decision.get("at") == 1:
                self.assertIsInstance(decision["weightedDominantShare"], float)
        self.assertEqual({d["weightedDominantShare"] for d in decisions if d.get("at") == 1}, {0.5})

        # metrics: exact resource accounting survives, dominantShare remains a rounded JSON number
        code, out, _ = run_cli(["metrics", "--cluster", cluster, "--tasks", tasks, "--queue-weights", weights])
        self.assertEqual(code, EXIT_OK)
        queues = json.loads(out)["metrics"]["queues"]
        self.assertEqual(list(queues), ["A", "Z"])
        self.assertEqual(queues["A"]["cpuTime"], (half - 2) * 10 + 2)
        self.assertEqual(queues["Z"]["cpuTime"], (half - 3) * 10 + 2)
        self.assertEqual(queues["A"]["dominantShare"], 0.5)

        # policies: both node selectors keep the same queue ordering (node choice is unchanged)
        code, out, _ = run_cli(["policies", "--cluster", cluster, "--tasks", tasks, "--queue-weights", weights])
        self.assertEqual(code, EXIT_OK)
        for entry in json.loads(out)["policies"]:
            self.assertEqual(entry["unplaced"], 0)

        # replay: the exact ordering is deterministic run to run
        code, out, _ = run_cli(["replay", "--cluster", cluster, "--tasks", tasks, "--queue-weights", weights])
        self.assertEqual(code, EXIT_OK)
        self.assertTrue(json.loads(out)["identical"])

        # best-fit changes only node selection, never the queue order
        code, out, _ = run_cli(
            ["trace", "--cluster", cluster, "--tasks", tasks, "--queue-weights", weights, "--policy", "best-fit"]
        )
        self.assertEqual(code, EXIT_OK)
        self.assertEqual([d["task"] for d in json.loads(out)["decisions"] if d.get("at") == 1 and "node" in d],
                         ["z1", "a1", "z2", "a2"])

            "missing": ['{"queue": "a"}'],
            "type": ['{"queue": "a", "weight": "2"}'],
            "unknown": ['{"queue": "a", "weight": 1, "extra": 2}'],
            "emptystring": ['{"queue": "", "weight": 1}'],
            "boolweight": ['{"queue": "a", "weight": true}'],
        }
        for name, lines in cases.items():

            with open(path, "w") as handle:

            code, out, err = run_cli(["metrics", "--cluster", self.cluster, "--tasks", tasks, "--queue-weights", path])
            self.assertEqual((code, out), (EXIT_ERROR, ""), name)
            document = json.loads(err)
            self.assertEqual(document["error"], "parse_error", name)
            self.assertEqual(document["line"], 2 if name in ("badjson", "nonobject") else 1, name)

570	    The scenarios use ~1e20 integer capacities: at that magnitude two fractions differing by a
571	    single unit of numerator map to the SAME IEEE double, so float ordering silently falls through
572	    to the queue/id tie-break. Every scenario below was observed to produce the wrong order on the
573	    float implementation and the right order on exact arithmetic. The displayed
574	    ``weightedDominantShare`` / ``dominantShare`` stay rounded to six decimals -- both exact values
575	    can print as one number without that changing who is picked first.
576	    """

585	        # Anchors leave queue Z one unit below queue A; each unit placed flips which queue is ahead,
586	        # so four same-tick placements must alternate z, a, z, a. Float shares are both 0.5 and the
587	        # old code served a1, a2, z1, z2 by queue name instead.
588	        tasks = (
589	            task("aRun", cpu=self.HALF - 2, memory=1, queue="A", duration=10),
590	            task("zRun", cpu=self.HALF - 3, memory=1, queue="Z", duration=10),
591	            task("z1", cpu=1, queue="Z", arrival=1),
592	            task("a1", cpu=1, queue="A", arrival=1),
593	            task("z2", cpu=1, queue="Z", arrival=1),
594	            task("a2", cpu=1, queue="A", arrival=1),
595	        )
596	        result = simulate(self.node(), tasks, queue_weights={"A": 1, "Z": 1})
597	        at_one = [entry["task"] for entry in result.decisions if "node" in entry and entry["at"] == 1]
598	        self.assertEqual(at_one, ["z1", "a1", "z2", "a2"])

600	        self.assertEqual({entry["weightedDominantShare"] for entry in result.decisions if entry.get("at") == 1}, {0.5})
